declared_source_and_boundary.center: for r<0.32 kpc, linearly extrapolate each component velocity as V(r)=V(0.32)*r/0.32, giving constant central rho; no central data supplied
declared_source_and_boundary.exterior: linearly taper inferred rho from its value at 44.08 kpc to zero across declared 5,10,20 kpc widths, then exact vacuum; inferred negative density is retained
declared_source_and_boundary.gas_convention: SPARC signed-force convention Vgas*abs(Vgas); literal positive square tested separately
declared_source_and_boundary.interpolator_baseline: PCHIP; natural cubic and Akima sensitivity runs
declared_source_and_boundary.outer_boundary: exact vacuum matching at R=44.08 kpc+taper; no observed outer velocity used as a boundary
declared_source_and_boundary.source_recipe: paper Eq. (47) pseudo-spherical inversion; interpolate Vdisk,Vgas then differentiate r*V_component^2

equations_and_units.isolated_robin: u'(R)=-(u(R)-1)/R, with vacuum u=1+B/r outside R

interpretation: No physical NGC 3198 prediction: the Eq. (47) pseudo-spherical source is negative over a robust band and SPARC Rotmod does not determine a unique 3-D source, center, or exterior taper. This tests only a predeclared mathematical surrogate.

leading_radial_growth_eigenvalue.D_factor: The physical growth rate is D times this per-D eigenvalue; D is not specified.
leading_radial_growth_eigenvalue.interpretation: negative is linearly decaying and positive growing only for the declared finite Robin realization; full-space diffusion has continuum spectrum reaching zero
leading_radial_growth_eigenvalue.method: P1 finite elements for q=r*delta_u, Dirichlet q(0)=0, Neumann q'(R)=0

limitations: The spherical inversion gives negative total density over 14.5-16.0 kpc for multiple interpolators; no clipping is allowed.
No local 3-D gas surface density, gas thickness, or source deprojection is staged.
Center extrapolation and outer taper are declared assumptions, not observed data.
Chi-square uses Rotmod errV only; no full covariance, inclination/distance systematics, or baryonic profile covariance is available.
This NGC 3198 is a diagnostic, not a holdout; success would not establish thermodynamic gravity or a relativistic cosmology.
